about.short: I'm Alikhan, a 16-year-old developer from Kostanay, Kazakhstan. I build AI-powered products — computer vision models, progressive web apps and Telegram bots — taking them from concept to deployment. I've competed in hackathons and pitch sessions across the Astana Hub ecosystem in Kostanay, Pavlodar and Almaty. My current project is Smart Green Qostanai, a service for monitoring urban tree health.
about.title: About me
body: I'm Alikhan. I'm 16, I live in Kostanay and I study in the maths stream of my lyceum.

My first technical project was in fifth grade — robotics, second place at the school showcase. Then came three years of doing nothing at all. My grades slid, and I dropped everything I had been working on. I'm not going to pretend otherwise: it is part of the story, and everything else grew out of it.

At the end of eighth grade I decided to start over. Over the following year I pulled my grades back up to nearly straight A's, finished music school alongside it — the final exams at both places ran at the same time — and landed in the environment that turned me around: hackathons, idea battles and pitch sessions across the Astana Hub ecosystem. Kostanay, Pavlodar, Almaty.

Now I build AI products. Computer vision, progressive web apps, Telegram bots, and work with LLMs — both local and cloud. What interests me is not the technology itself but the moment it turns into a working service somebody actually uses.
My current project is Smart Green Qostanai: a PWA that assesses the condition of a city tree from a photograph. Built at the Qostanai Smart City hackathon.
Next comes an undergraduate degree abroad. First priority is Japan, through the MEXT programme.
